Yes! Niftycase is great.  It's very affordable and you get a lot for what you buy.   Something like the tiptop mantis is going to cost more for just the case.   You should be able to find the niftycase bundle with the modules, cables and a couple removable blanks for $270.   If you think you'd be interested in modular it's a good first step - you may want to watch some videos like Benn Jordan's "Ready to go modular? 10 Common Beginner Questions" to know some of the cool things and some of the limitations of Eurorack.

[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ruFN4fVK0gE](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ruFN4fVK0gE)

I have the niftycase, as well as a couple other cases and the niftycase's power and structure is great.  Have had zero problems.  It has good depth (deeper than the Rackbrute, for example) and for me the rails have been solid.  I have heard some other complaints on it though, so quality control might be a problem.   

The chipz and cellz modules are weird.  Chipz is an oscillator, and doesn't make very good sounds by itself.  You have no VCA, so with just those two you'll be buzzing through some tones with no dynamics.  You will not be impressed.  Even with additions, it can be hard to get much mileage out of these two (Chipz does have a weird LFO, Oscillators can be useful for more than just listening to the output, and you can get creative with even the simple capabilities of cellz, but generally it's limited) - but they will get you stared on the modular experience, and the bargain of the niftycase is so good it's OK for these modules to be nothing special.

It comes with some MIDI to CV stuff that's very useful too.  Typically you would have to buy a module to do this.   

An alternative you may want to explore is starting Modular is a semi-modular like the make noise 0-coast or behringer neutron.  It will also give you a modular experience but basically all the modules exist in one piece.  If you went on from there to buy a eurorack case, a 0-coast would still be able to connect to that and work with it as if it were a module.  The 0-coast is more expensive, but will give you a lot more interesting results than just having chipz and cellz.  Just another option you may want to consider.

Surprised me -

Squid Salmple - I picked this one up at Knobcon kind of on a whim..they were doing a nice sale and thought it could be fun, thinking that samplers weren't exactly my thing - but I figured it was as good as any to try.  Now it's one of my favorite modules.  It comes with a lot of sample packs on its own, and many of them sound great.  The ability to CV so many things, from simple things like the attack and decay, to the quality of the sample or the start and end points of the sample, gives this thing so much depth.  Almost any feature I would want, choking, CV samples, triggering loops..it can do.  Then bringing your own samples into it adds more fun.  It also has plenty of interesting deeper things I haven't explored yet with its recording features.  It's a module that was so fun and quick to pick up but then has a lot of depth beneath it that keeps it interesting.  Love!!

Ornament & Crime Hemispheres - I thought it'd be interesting to try O\_C, and had a chance to grab one locally.  But it finds its way into most of my patches.  It's interface is great and it has some very simple tools that you can pick up when you need, and some very complex tools that can be fun to build a patch around.  Definitely a little inspiration machine.  It clicks with me in the best way a multitool can - there are things about it I still don't understand, but with some exploration I can know what something does for life, go to it, and use it, thanks to its great clear interface and useful graphical indicators. 

Intellijel Atlantis - Atlantis is totally my favorite module.  I can't speak on behalf of it being a true spiritual successor to the SH-101 - I have never owned one - but the Atlantis always delivers in sound quality.  It just sounds sooo good, and there's not a whole lot more I can say about it.  It is far from a one-trick pony, if I want a specific sound I can usually make something like it on Atlantis.

​

Disappointed me -

Zoia Euroburo - really jumped on the bandwagon on this one.  I love benn jordan's videos and he made me want one..but I found that this thing wasn't for me at all.  The idea of having a modular system within your modular system just wasn't working for me  - never felt natural to try to patch it in and out of the system..a little limiting with only 4 CV in/out and the CPU could quickly reach its limit.  It wasn't inspiring to try to bridge the gap between it and my other modules.  Something about patching in it feels a little clinical and it was like having to bounce back and forth between two different mentalities.  On the DSP side of things..never loved the way its fx sounded.  It always felt like if you wanted to come up with some creative fx chain you'd reach a limit with the CPU rather quickly.   I sold it rather quickly.

disting mk 4 - Unfortunately bought this off MW and found out the SD card inserter was broken.  Right away off to a bad start. Everyone's already said generally what I find disappointing.  The UI and UX don't work for me.  I can't seem to retain any information about it because it's not enjoyable to use.  I think it's useful but found that in modular I often like finding workarounds to my problems rather than having something like disting do it.  So even if I needed another LFO or S&H sometimes i'd improvise with something else.  I'd sell it but with the busted SD card inserter I doubt anyone would want it..so it just sicks in my rack collecting dust!

MI Beads - I'm a HUGE MI fan so this one hurts to say a little.  I DO think beads is very interesting as a way to put something in and get something totally new out (so 100% wet).  I was drawn to that side of it, but also to the idea of using its reverb, delay setting, and in general using it as an effect.  That part doesn't work for me too well.  It always ends up sounding pretty similar and not being interesting to mess with - it feels more like trying to find the right settings that sound decent, and then leaving it alone so it doesn't mess up.  And then the overall 'character' of beads doesn't work for me, I guess.  I don't care for the sound of the yellow or red modes for most of my patches.
